messages.subject: Compiling rJava for Java7 on a mac
messages.subject_clean: Compiling rJava for Java7 on a mac
messages.body_plain:
I am running:

Mac OS 10.8.4,
R 3.1.0,
rJava 0.9.6,
RStudio 0.98

I would like to compile rJava from source so that it can run Java 1.7,
ideally from within RStudio. Have read a number of websites giving advice
about reconfiguring R for 1.7 and setting compiler flags (
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/13610293/how-to-get-rjava-0-9-3-to-work-on-os-x-10-7-4-with-oracle-java-1-7),
but when I try install.packages("rJava",type='source'), I continue to run
into:

... checking JNI data types... configure: error: One or more JNI types
differ from the corresponding native type. You may need to use non-standard
compiler flags or a different compiler in order to fix this.
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘rJava’

Any advice would be greatly appreciated, particularly step-by-step help.

Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: Parallel computing with Rserve
messages.body_plain:
On Sep 30, 2014, at 9:33 AM, hseshadri <hemaseshadri at gmail.com> wrote:

> Will Rserve work with doParallel and snow packages? 

Yes


> I understand you can use Java's multithreading to improve the computing speed 
> per machine since Rserve can fork new process for each client. I want to 
> incorporate multiple machines to reduce the computation time. Can I still use 
> Rserve? What packages will work with Rserve well.
> 

Yes. The only issue you have to be aware of is that fork() shares all descriptors, so you don't want to create clusters in the server, you only want to do it once you forked an instance for the client such that multiple clients don't bash each other's connections.

Cheers,
S
